text:
Maria: Quick question — if we change the demote path to emit a "soft-demote" token instead of immediate eviction, can we guarantee read-after-write for in-flight requests when ownership flips?
Josh: You mean like a two-phase demote where soft-demote prevents new prefetches but keeps KV residency for N seconds?
Maria: Exactly. Keep residency + a grace counter so RPCs that already saw the prefix can continue to use it. New RPCs get routed to fallback or fetch.
Lee: That could help hotkey churn. But what about memory accounting? We may hold memory longer and blow slab budgets.
Sam: We can limit soft-demote with a TTL and a max-refcount threshold per prefix. If exceeded, fall back to synchronous handoff.
Josh: Sketch of the flow:
```
owner receives demote request -> mark prefix SOFT_DEMOTED, grace_deadline = now + ttl
inflight reads continue, new prefetch requests are rejected or redirected
periodic sweep: if refcount==0 or now>grace_deadline -> complete demote (evict)
```
Anya: Who handles the redirection? Router or owner? Router seems more scalable but needs lease visibility.
Maria: Router already keeps a lease map for routing. We could add a soft-demote flag to the lease metadata and short-circuit prefetch admission.
Lee: Concern: lease metadata staleness across replicas. If router misses soft-demote it will still send prefetches -> owner will reject, but that adds extra RPCs and latency.
Sam: Rejection path could return a lightweight hint header (e.g., X-Prefix-Demoted: true) so routers quickly add a local cache entry for TTL. That reduces repeated rejects.
sre-bot: Deploy note: Canary will flip soft-demote on 5% of hosts in shard 4 between 03:00–06:00 UTC.
Josh: Metrics we should track in canary: prefix grace hold time, reject->success retry count, slab usage delta, tail latency for requests touching demoted prefixes.
Maria: + count of preseved KV hits (how many reads served from soft-demoted vs fallback).
Anya: Also track cross-tenant fairness: are some tenants abusing soft-demote to hog memory? Add per-tenant soft-demote bytes gauge.
Lee: We should add an admission control config: max_soft_demote_total_bytes and per-tenant cap. If exceeded, fail demote to immediate evict (fail-open).
Sam: For correctness, need to ensure demote completion is linearizable with ongoing writes. Proposal: writes acquire a small demote-guard token; if demote started, writers either wait for demote to finish or bump refcount.
Maria: Bumping refcount for writers seems simpler: writer increments refcount via CAS before applying. But a slow writer could keep prefix alive forever.
Josh: Add a max_writer_hold window: writer bump has a per-write TTL. After TTL writes no longer keep prefix alive.
Anya: Edge case: owner dies during soft-demote. Handoff must consider grace_deadline. New owner must inherit the grace_deadline or treat as completed. Which is safer?
Lee: Safer to treat as accelerated completion during owner takeover to avoid holding stale memory. But only if we can guarantee no writers are mid-flight; otherwise we'd violate RA write.
Sam: We can record a demote_epoch id with the lease. New owner reads epoch and checks persisted refcount snapshot. If snapshot shows inflight>0, new owner delays completion for a short backoff.
Maria: That implies we need a tiny persistent demote marker in the lease store (TTL-backed) so takeovers see demote state. Slightly increases metadata ops but only on demote events.
Josh: For the canary, implement a non-persistent mode first (owner-local) and monitor takeover cases. If we see rare correctness errors, promote to persisted marker.
Anya: Sounds reasonable. Quick win if we can reduce churn without extra lease ops.
Lee: One more: update observability — add "soft_demote.rejections" counter and a sample log on demote completion showing reason (ttl, refcount, takeover).
Maria: I'll draft a tiny RFC with the state machine and metric list. Can we agree to the experiment shape: 5% canary, soft-demote TTL 10s, per-tenant cap 50MB, global cap 5GB?
Josh: +1 for those starting numbers. We'll iterate after metrics.
Sam: I'll add router hint header and local negative cache for 30s to reduce reject storms.
Anya: I'll prepare the canary rollout playbook (rollback criteria: >0.5% increase in p99 tail or any RA-write inconsistency).
Maria: Thanks — I'll open the RFC and link the PR. :rocket:
